title: “Short is the Road that Leads from Fear to Hate”: Fear Speech in Indian WhatsApp Groups
findings: Fear speech against Muslims in Indian WhatsApp groups is prevalent, spreads faster and has a longer lifetime than non-fear speech messages. This type of speech is significantly less toxic than traditional hate speech, making it difficult for standard NLP models to detect (the best model, XLM-Roberta, achieved a macro F1-score of 0.71). Users who post fear speech tend to occupy central positions in their social networks, enhancing message dissemination. A survey of these users revealed they are more likely to believe and share fear-related statements and support anti-Muslim political issues compared to control groups.

measurement_description: Detection and characterization of 'fear speech' against Muslims in Indian political WhatsApp groups. The benchmark measures the ability of NLP models to classify text messages as containing fear speech, a subtle form of harmful speech aimed at instilling existential fear of a target religious group.
